vision: An AI-powered bridge between physical documents and digital business systems: photograph a document, extract accurate structured data with AI, review anything uncertain, and push clean records into the software the business already uses.
problem: Manual data entry from paper forms, receipts, invoices and ID documents into spreadsheets, databases and business software is slow, expensive and error-prone.
targetUsers: Small business back-office staff who retype invoices and receipts
Finance and accounting teams processing high document volumes
Field agents capturing forms and IDs on mobile devices
Enterprise integration teams needing an audited ingestion pipeline
Developers building on the platform API and connector marketplace

currentState.summary: M1 and M2 are complete; the Phase 3 tail is largely done too — CRM/ERP/accounting connectors, a signed connector marketplace with permission disclosure and rollback, and automatic page detection on mobile. Remaining: workflow automation (AGENT-001), voice assistance (VOICE-001) and the desktop translation sweep (I18N-001).

statusLegend.done: Implemented, tested and verified against its acceptance criteria.
statusLegend.in_progress: Actively being built; may be partially working.
statusLegend.pending: Not started. Ready to be picked up if dependencies are done.
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed until the blocking item or decision is resolved.
statusLegend.deferred: Consciously pushed beyond the current phase.

definitionOfDone: Acceptance criteria for the story are all satisfied.
Code is typed, linted and formatted with no new warnings.
Automated tests cover the new behaviour and pass locally.
Manual test case in TESTING.md (if one exists for the story) is executed.
No secrets, credentials or personal data are committed.
Documentation touched by the change is updated (API.md, DATABASE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md as applicable).
Status in PRD.json is updated and AGENT_STATE.md reflects reality.

epics.title: Foundation, tooling and documentation
epics.description: Repository conventions, dependency baseline, documentation pack, CI and code quality gates.

epics.title: QR device pairing and secure device channel

epics.title: Mobile document capture

epics.title: Desktop application
epics.description: Cross-platform desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux) to receive scans, review extractions and manage connectors and exports.

epics.title: AI document intelligence
epics.description: Text extraction, structure understanding, table detection, classification, field recognition and confidence scoring.

epics.title: Universal Data Model
epics.description: Canonical, versioned, validated internal representation of every extracted record before it reaches any external system.

epics.title: Human-in-the-loop review
epics.description: UI and workflow for reviewing low-confidence fields, correcting values and approving records.

epics.title: Excel and CSV export

epics.title: Connector platform
epics.description: Plugin-based connectors with create/read/update/search capabilities for Google Sheets, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite.

epics.title: Data mapping and learning
epics.description: Map extracted fields to destination fields and learn from human corrections over time.

epics.title: Document template builder
epics.description: Define reusable document templates and expected fields to improve extraction accuracy.

epics.title: Teams, projects and collaboration
epics.description: Organisations, projects, roles, batch processing and team review queues.

epics.title: Security, audit and compliance
epics.description: Authentication, authorisation, encryption, retention controls and immutable audit trails.

epics.title: Enterprise integrations and API platform
epics.description: CRM, ERP and accounting integrations, public developer API, connector marketplace and AI business agents.

epics.title: Analytics, i18n and assistant features
epics.description: Analytics dashboard, multi-language support, voice commands and smart camera assistance.

stories.title: Repository and dependency baseline
stories.description: Git repository initialised with a React Native dependency manifest (react-native 0.86, react 19, React Navigation, socket.io-client) and a lockfile.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json and package-lock.json are committed.
Core dependencies install reproducibly with npm ci / npm install.
A .gitignore excludes node_modules, secrets and build output.

stories.title: Project documentation pack
stories.description: Single source of truth documentation set: PRD.json, REQUIREMENTS.md, AI.md, AGENT_STATE.md, TASKS.md, CHANGELOG.md, DECISIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, DATABASE.md, API.md, TESTING.md, SECURITY.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, ENVIRONMENT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md, LICENSE and .env.example.
acceptanceCriteria: Every document exists at the repository root and is internally consistent.
PRD.json is valid JSON and parses without error.
Story statuses in PRD.json match reality.
No real credentials appear in any documented example.

stories.title: Monorepo restructuring and TypeScript baseline
stories.description: Move to the target workspace layout (apps/mobile, apps/desktop, apps/backend, packages/shared, packages/connectors) with TypeScript, path aliases and shared tsconfig.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspaces defined in root package.json and installs work from a clean clone.
Each workspace has a tsconfig extending the shared base and compiles with tsc --noEmit.
Existing React Native dependencies keep working from apps/mobile.

stories.title: Linting, formatting and test harness
stories.description: ESLint + Prettier configuration, Jest projects for backend/shared and React Native Testing Library for mobile, plus a standard npm script surface.
acceptanceCriteria: npm run lint, npm run format:check and npm test succeed on a clean clone.
Mobile component tests can render the app root.
Backend unit tests can run a trivial passing suite.

stories.title: Continuous integration pipeline
stories.description: GitHub Actions workflow running install, typecheck, lint, tests and PRD.json validation on every pull request.
acceptanceCriteria: Pull requests show a passing CI check.
Failing typecheck, lint or tests block merge.
PRD.json is validated as JSON in CI.

stories.title: Backend API skeleton
stories.description: Node.js + TypeScript HTTP service with health endpoint, config loader, structured logging, request validation and central error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/v1/health returns 200 with version and uptime.
Configuration is read from environment variables via a validating schema.
Unknown routes return a consistent JSON error envelope.
Service starts with npm run dev from apps/backend.

stories.title: Database schema and migrations
stories.description: PostgreSQL schema managed by migrations, covering organisations, users, devices, pairing sessions, documents, extractions, review, connectors, mappings, jobs and audit logs (see DATABASE.md).
acceptanceCriteria: Migrations run forward and back cleanly on an empty database.
Every table has a primary key and timestamps.
Foreign keys and unique constraints from DATABASE.md are enforced.
A seed script creates one demo organisation and user.

stories.title: User authentication and sessions
stories.description: Email and password registration and login with Argon2id hashing, short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens; logout revokes sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes.
Access tokens expire within 15 minutes; refresh tokens rotate and are revocable.
Login is rate limited and returns generic errors that do not reveal whether an email exists.
Protected endpoints reject missing, expired or invalid tokens with 401.

stories.title: Role-based access control
stories.description: Organisation-scoped roles (owner, admin, reviewer, operator, viewer) enforced on every API route and reflected in the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Every data query is scoped to the caller's organisation.
Role checks are enforced server-side and covered by tests.
Forbidden actions return 403 with a stable error code.

stories.title: Desktop-generated QR pairing code
stories.description: The desktop client requests a single-use pairing session from the backend and renders it as a QR code containing only a short-lived pairing token and endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: Pairing token is cryptographically random, single-use and expires within 2 minutes.
Expired or reused tokens are rejected with a clear error.
QR payload contains no long-lived secret and no personal data.

stories.title: Mobile QR scan and device authentication
stories.description: The mobile app scans the desktop QR code, exchanges the pairing token for a device credential and completes mutual authentication with the backend.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid QR code pairs the phone in under 5 seconds on a normal network.
Device credentials are stored in platform secure storage, never in plain async storage.
Scanning an expired, tampered or previously used code shows a friendly failure and allows retry.
On successful pairing the desktop shows the connected device name and platform.

stories.title: Encrypted realtime device channel
stories.description: Socket.IO channel authenticated by device credentials, used for jobs, progress events and status updates between mobile, backend and desktop; all traffic over TLS.
acceptanceCriteria: Unauthenticated socket connections are refused.
Reconnect resumes correctly without duplicating jobs.
Progress events arrive on the desktop within 1 second of backend state change.
Message sizes and event names are documented in API.md.

stories.title: Device management and revocation
stories.description: Users can list paired devices, rename them and revoke access; revocation immediately invalidates tokens and closes sockets.
acceptanceCriteria: Revoking a device invalidates its credentials within one request.
Revoked devices cannot re-authenticate with stored tokens.
Device list shows name, platform, last seen and paired date.

stories.title: Mobile app shell and navigation
stories.description: React Native application for Android and iOS with React Navigation (stack + bottom tabs), theming, error boundary and offline banner.
acceptanceCriteria: App builds and launches on both Android and iOS simulators.
Navigation covers pairing, capture, queue, review and settings.
App renders a friendly state when the backend is unreachable.

stories.title: Camera capture with edge detection and enhancement
stories.description: In-app camera with document edge detection, crop, perspective correction, rotation and basic enhancement (contrast/shadow removal) before upload.
acceptanceCriteria: User can capture, crop and retake a document page.
Uploaded image is an upright, cropped, compressed JPEG under 2 MB where possible.
Capture works without network connectivity and queues locally.

stories.title: Offline-first upload queue
stories.description: Captured pages are persisted locally and uploaded reliably with retry, exponential backoff, resumable progress and duplicate protection.
acceptanceCriteria: Queue survives app restart.
Failed uploads retry automatically without user action.
Same local capture is never uploaded twice (idempotency key).
User can see per-item upload status.

stories.title: Document upload API and storage
stories.description: Authenticated endpoint accepts document images (or PDFs), validates type and size, stores originals in object storage with server-side encryption and records metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Only allowed MIME types are accepted; content is sniffed, not trusted from headers.
Files over the configured limit are rejected with 413.
Every stored object is addressable only through the API with authorisation checks.
Uploads are idempotent per client-supplied key.

stories.title: OCR and text extraction pipeline
stories.description: Asynchronous job pipeline that runs OCR (with a local engine as default and a cloud provider as an option) and stores per-page text with word-level geometry.
acceptanceCriteria: Jobs run asynchronously with status transitions queued → running → succeeded/failed.
Failures are retried with backoff and surface an actionable error message.
Per-page text and geometry are persisted for downstream extraction.
Average invoice-sized page processes in under 10 seconds in the reference environment.

stories.title: Document classification
stories.description: Classify each document into form, receipt, invoice, ID, contract, table or handwritten and store a confidence score.
acceptanceCriteria: Classifier returns the document type plus a 0–1 confidence.
Low-confidence classifications are flagged for human review.
Classification accuracy meets the agreed benchmark on the labelled test set.

stories.title: Field, table and key-value extraction with confidence
stories.description: Extract structured fields, tables and key-value pairs into the Universal Data Model with per-field confidence, source geometry and provider provenance.
acceptanceCriteria: Every extracted field carries a value, confidence and source region.
Tables are preserved as rows and columns, not flattened text.
Fields below the review threshold are marked needs_review.
Provider output is validated against the UDM schema before it is persisted.

stories.title: Provider-agnostic AI abstraction
stories.description: A single internal interface for OCR and extraction so local and cloud providers, and their models, can be swapped by configuration without touching business logic.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one local and one cloud provider implement the interface.
No provider SDK types leak outside the adapter layer.
Per-request timeout, retry and cost/latency logging are supported.
Local AI mode works with no outbound internet access.

stories.title: Universal Data Model schema and validation
stories.description: Versioned canonical JSON schema (validated at runtime with Zod, published as JSON Schema) representing any captured record: document type, fields, tables, provenance and confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Schema is versioned and backwards compatible within a major version.
Invalid payloads are rejected with field-level errors.
The same schema is used by mobile, backend and desktop through packages/shared.
Published JSON Schema is documented in DATABASE.md.

stories.title: Human-in-the-loop review interface
stories.description: Side-by-side document image and extracted fields where users can confirm, correct or reject values, with keyboard-first navigation and confidence highlighting.
acceptanceCriteria: Low-confidence fields are visually distinguished and sorted first.
Editing a value requires no more than one click plus typing.
Every change is recorded with before/after values and the acting user.
Records can be approved only when all required fields are present.

stories.title: Correction capture for learning
stories.description: Store human corrections in a structured form usable for field mapping suggestions and future model or prompt improvements.
acceptanceCriteria: Corrections store document type, field, original value, corrected value and confidence.
No correction data is used for training without explicit opt-in.
Correction statistics are queryable per organisation.

stories.title: Excel (.xlsx) export
stories.description: Export approved records to a formatted .xlsx workbook with selectable columns, one sheet per document type and a provenance column.
acceptanceCriteria: Workbook opens cleanly in Excel, LibreOffice and Google Sheets.
Table fields are exported as structured rows.
Export of 1,000 records completes in under 30 seconds.
Empty exports produce a valid file with headers only.

stories.title: CSV export
stories.description: RFC 4180 compliant CSV export with UTF-8 BOM option, configurable delimiter, quote escaping and formula-injection protection.
acceptanceCriteria: Values containing delimiters, quotes or newlines round-trip correctly.
Leading =, +, - and @ are neutralised to prevent spreadsheet formula injection.
Delimiter and encoding options are respected.

stories.title: Desktop application shell
stories.description: Electron desktop client for Windows, macOS and Linux with secure defaults (context isolation, no remote module, explicit IPC allow-list) and auto-update plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: Packaged builds launch on all three platforms.
Renderer has no direct Node or filesystem access; IPC is allow-listed and validated.
App stores tokens in the OS keychain.
Auto-update checks can be disabled by configuration.

stories.title: Desktop review and job dashboard
stories.description: Dashboard listing incoming documents, live processing status and review queues, with bulk approve and export actions.
acceptanceCriteria: New uploads appear without manual refresh.
Bulk approve skips records with unresolved low-confidence fields.
Filters cover status, document type, date and device.

stories.title: Connector plugin interface and SDK
stories.description: Documented connector contract with manifest, capability declaration (create/read/update/search), schema discovery and health check, plus a local connector runner.
acceptanceCriteria: A new connector can be added without changing core code.
Connector contract is typed and covered by contract tests.
Failing connectors are isolated and reported, not crashing the app.

stories.title: Google Sheets connector
stories.description: OAuth-based Google Sheets connector supporting append, update and read with column mapping and header detection.
acceptanceCriteria: OAuth tokens are stored encrypted and refreshed automatically.
Append respects existing headers and never overwrites unrelated columns.
Revoked access surfaces a clear re-authentication prompt.

stories.title: MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite connectors
stories.description: Database connectors with schema introspection, mapped inserts/updates and configurable conflict handling.
acceptanceCriteria: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned by the API.
Introspection lists tables and columns for mapping.
Writes run in transactions and roll back on failure.
Read-only credentials prevent writes at the database level too.

stories.title: Field mapping between UDM and destinations
stories.description: Visual mapping from UDM fields to destination fields with type transforms, defaults, required-field validation and reusable mapping profiles.
acceptanceCriteria: Mapping is saved per connector and reusable across exports.
Type conversions (date, number, boolean) are deterministic and tested.
Unmapped required destination fields block activation with a clear message.

stories.title: Duplicate detection and merge
stories.description: Detect likely duplicates using configurable keys and fuzzy matching, then append, update, merge or skip according to policy.
acceptanceCriteria: User can configure duplicate keys per connector.
Matches show a similarity score and the fields that matched.
Merge never silently discards reviewed values.

stories.title: Document template builder
stories.description: Define reusable document templates with expected fields, sample pages and validation rules to steer extraction.
acceptanceCriteria: Templates can be created from an uploaded sample or from scratch.
Extraction uses the matching template when one exists.
Templates are versioned and can be disabled without data loss.

stories.title: Batch processing
stories.description: Upload and process many documents at once with progress, partial failure handling and per-item results.
acceptanceCriteria: Batches of 100 documents are queued and monitored.
A failed item does not fail the batch.
Progress and results are exportable.

stories.title: Organisations, projects and team roles
stories.description: Multi-tenant organisations with projects, invitations, role assignment and review assignment.
acceptanceCriteria: Users cannot see data from another organisation under any route.
Invitations expire and are single-use.
Role changes take effect on the next request.

stories.title: Immutable audit trail
stories.description: Append-only audit log of authentication, document access, review changes, exports and connector writes, with actor, tenant, IP and timestamp.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit records cannot be updated or deleted through the application.
Every privileged action emits exactly one audit record.
Audit log is searchable by actor, action and date range.

stories.title: Data retention and deletion controls
stories.description: Configurable retention for originals and extracted data, plus a verified deletion path that purges storage objects and database rows.
acceptanceCriteria: Admins can set retention per organisation.
Expired documents are purged by a scheduled job and the purge is logged.
Deletion removes objects from storage, not just metadata.
Exports of deleted documents are no longer possible.

stories.title: Developer API and API keys
stories.description: Public, versioned REST API for documents, extractions and exports, authenticated with scoped API keys, documented in API.md with examples.
acceptanceCriteria: API keys are shown once, hashed at rest and revocable.
Scopes restrict each key to declared actions.
OpenAPI document is published and validated in CI.

stories.title: CRM, ERP and accounting connectors
stories.description: First-party connectors for at least one CRM, one ERP and one accounting system, following the connector contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Each connector implements create/read/update/search.
Field mapping works without code changes.
Errors are translated into actionable user messages.

stories.title: Connector marketplace
stories.description: Discover, install and update third-party connectors with review, signing and permission disclosure.
acceptanceCriteria: Installed connectors declare and display required permissions.
Unsigned or revoked connectors cannot be installed.
Updates can be rolled back.

stories.title: Workflow automation and AI business agents
stories.description: Rule and agent driven workflows, e.g. invoice uploaded → extracted → validated → saved to accounting → user notified.
acceptanceCriteria: Workflows can be created from a visual builder.
Each run is logged with inputs, outputs and failures.
Agents cannot perform destructive actions without an approval policy.

stories.title: Analytics dashboard
stories.description: Volume, accuracy, review time, connector success rate and cost per document, filterable by project and period.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboards load in under 2 seconds for 90 days of data.
Metrics are computed from auditable records.
Figures can be exported.

stories.title: Multi-language support
stories.description: Externalised strings, locale-aware dates/numbers and right-to-left layout support across mobile and desktop.
acceptanceCriteria: No user-facing string is hardcoded in components.
At least two locales ship and switch at runtime.
RTL layouts render without clipped controls.

stories.title: Voice commands and smart camera assistance
stories.description: Hands-free capture guidance (steady, move closer, page detected) and voice commands for common capture and review actions.
acceptanceCriteria: Camera guidance works fully offline.
Voice commands can be disabled and require explicit permission.
No audio is stored or transmitted without consent.

openQuestions.question: Which AI/OCR providers are approved for production, and is there a budget cap per document?
Is the product commercially licensed (proprietary) or open source? LICENSE.md currently assumes proprietary.
Which regions/customers must be supported first, and what data-residency requirements apply?
Should the desktop client work standalone (local-only mode) without a hosted backend?
